:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.9`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useExpectToStrictEqual`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`test`](/linter/domains#test)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`jest/prefer-strict-equal`](https://github.com/jest-community/eslint-plugin-jest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-strict-equal.md)
  - Same as [`vitest/prefer-strict-equal`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/eslint-plugin-vitest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-strict-equal.md)
  - Same as [`playwright/prefer-strict-equal`](https://github.com/playwright-community/eslint-plugin-playwright/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-strict-equal.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useExpectToStrictEqual": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce using `toStrictEqual()` instead of `toEqual()` to compare values in tests.

`toEqual()` ignores some differences between the two values it compares:

- A property set to `undefined` is treated the same as a property that doesn't exist.
- An empty slot in an array is treated the same as an item set to `undefined`.
- An object created from a class is treated the same as a plain object with the same
properties.

`toEqual()` can therefore treat two different values as equal. `toStrictEqual()` checks
all of these differences.

The fix is unsafe because it can change the result of a test.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
expect({ a: "a", b: undefined }).toEqual({ a: "a" });
```
